feature.summary: Per-agent memory, routines, a private workspace and a responsibility list. The brief calls all four missing. The code has two partial pieces on web and mobile Cloud: routines that run as an agent (Deployments), and up to 20 reference files per agent. No per-agent memory, no private computer and no responsibility list were found.

purpose.what_it_does: Would give each agent its own memory, scheduled routines, a workspace for its files and a list of what it owns. Today Cloud agents can own scheduled routines and carry reference files; nothing else of the four is built.
purpose.why_it_exists: S61.06, S61.07, S61.10 and S61.12 describe agents that persist over time like a team member (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and mobile Cloud users who want an agent that runs on a schedule or reads fixed files; future users of persistent agents.
problems_solved: Running the same agent on a schedule without opening a chat.
Giving an agent reference material once instead of attaching it each chat.
use_cases: Add a weekly routine that runs a research agent every Monday.
Upload a style guide as Knowledge so a writing agent always has it.
See the agent's recent chats and routines under Activity.

Persistent private workspace or computer per agent (S61.10): none found.
Responsibility list per agent (S61.12): none found.
CLI agents have no memory, routines, workspace or responsibilities; the CLI has cron tools but they are not tied to an agent (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs:1204-1218).

established.statement: Each agent keeps its own memory separate from other agents.
An agent can own routines that run as that agent.
Each agent has its own persistent workspace or computer where its files live.
Each agent shows the list of responsibilities it currently owns.
Memory, projects and context are governed by their own system page.

acceptance_criteria: A routine created with agent=<id> runs with that agent's instructions, model and tool toggles.
A paused or retired agent's routine run fails with the unavailable message instead of running.
Adding a file with an existing name is refused.
Reference file text appears in the model context but is labelled as material, not instructions.
Total reference text per turn never exceeds 120,000 characters.
inferred: Per-agent memory must respect Local, own-key and Cloud boundaries (AGENTS.md section 6) [inferred].
The activity panel is the closest thing to a responsibility list and could be extended [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add a memory scope keyed by agent id.
[proposed] Show owned routines, open runs and open tasks as responsibilities.
[proposed] Let an agent have a sandbox folder in Cloud with file read and write.

steps.what_happens: Upload: the owner's file text is stored with a SHA-256 hash and size after the 20-file check.
Each chat turn as the agent loads the files in name order and cuts them at 120,000 characters.
A routine fires; the executor loads the agent, refuses when paused or retired, uses the agent's model and tool settings.
Activity reads conversations and scheduled tasks linked to the agent for this viewer.

corrections.claim: Scheduled routines skip the daily message count (schedule-service.ts:922-924) [inferred].
corrections.what_the_code_shows: schedule-service.ts:922-924 is assertScheduleAgent, which passes countTurns:false only when a routine is created or edited. At run time scheduled-agent-executor.ts:~899-901 calls loadAgentTurnConfig(scope.db, scope.userId, task.agentId) with the default countTurns:true. That default enforces dailyTurnLimit (agent-turn-config.ts:78-86) and monthlyCreditLimit (agent-turn-config.ts:87-95), and the executor throws ScheduledAgentUnavailableError when either is hit.
corrections.correction: Routine runs count against the agent's daily message limit and monthly credit limit, and are refused when either is reached. Only the check made when a routine is created or edited skips the count.

corrections.claim: Subscription: No plan check found in the files or activity routes. Scheduled routines may have their own limits in the schedule service (not opened).
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The files and activity routes show no plan check, so that part holds. The routine run path does check the plan. The executor resolves the entitlement bundle and calls evaluateManagedComputeAccess(... 'schedules'). When access is denied the run is skipped and returns 'Scheduled execution skipped: <reason>'.
corrections.correction: Files and activity have no plan gate. Routine runs as an agent are gated by the managed-compute access policy for 'schedules', and the plan tier is passed into schedule validation and routing.

corrections.claim: A routine uses the agent's model when set, else the task's model (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:923).
corrections.what_the_code_shows: agentModelFor returns the agent's model only when the task model is empty or an Auto id. If the task names a specific model, that model wins. If the agent has no model, the task's model is used.
corrections.correction: A routine uses the agent's model only when the task's own model is unset or Auto. An explicit task model overrides it.

corrections.claim: Only the owner uploads or removes files and only an active agent accepts new files; Retired agent: files cannot be added.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: addAgentFile calls requireOwnedAgent, then assertEditable. assertEditable rejects only status 'retired'. A paused agent still accepts files. Owner-only is correct for add and delete.
corrections.correction: Only the owner can add or remove files. Adding is refused only for a retired agent, and a paused agent still accepts files.

corrections.what_the_code_shows: The values are right: AGENT_FILES_MAX = 20 and AGENT_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 512_000. They sit at lines 25-26, and lines 22-23 hold other constants (AGENT_DAILY_TURN_LIMIT_MAX, AGENT_MONTHLY_CREDIT_LIMIT_MAX). Enforcement of the 20-file limit is at custom-agent-service.ts:773-777. I did not find where the byte cap is enforced.
corrections.correction: Cite agents.ts:25-26. The byte cap enforcement site was not located (the files route was not checked).

missing_facts: Per-agent dailyTurnLimit and monthlyCreditLimit (owner-set) are enforced on routine runs and on chat turns, with the messages 'reached its limit of N messages a day' and 'used the N credits its owner allows each month' (apps/web/lib/agents/agent-turn-config.ts:78-95). The page lists neither in Limits and metering.

Routine runs are gated by evaluateManagedComputeAccess for 'schedules' with the user's entitlement plan, and are skipped with 'Scheduled execution skipped: ...' when denied (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:~889-912).

A routine as an agent also applies the agent's web search, code execution, connector selection and allowed or blocked web domains, not only its model (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:~938-960).
